$comment: Derived artifacts of spec inputs (T0012). A task whose allowed_scope covers a marker input MUST also cover the derived artifact: pre-dispatch scope validation fails the spawn otherwise, and collect treats the derived artifact of a covered marker as in scope (so a Worker can regenerate it without an out-of-scope rejection). The pairs mirror scripts/speclib.py derive_spec_version: inputs are tasks/tasks.json plus every file under specs/ except the marker itself.

rules.note: every spec file is an input of the derived spec version marker
the task DAG is an input of the derived spec version marker

The canonical schema snapshot is generated from the migration history (scripts/gen_schema_snapshot.py). It is a derived artifact, not a product spec a Worker edits by judgement: a task whose scope covers infra/migrations/** regenerates it mechanically, and CI fails when the two diverge. This is the auditable path for schema evolution, and it is the whole of the Worker's access to specs/.

The sqlc output (sqlc.yaml: schema infra/migrations, queries internal/persistence/queries). Checked in, regenerated by scripts/gen_sqlc.sh, and CI fails when it drifts (tests/integration/check-sqlc-drift.sh). It is declared so the artifact is REGENERATED rather than merged as text: a task and main both regenerate it, and their two copies differ on every line the other one added, so a textual apply refuses on context alone even when the changes are nowhere near each other — T0209's querier.go, where the task's rsg query methods and main's policy methods interleave alphabetically. The marker is the queries directory and not infra/migrations/** even though the migrations are the other input: a migration-only change leaves this output byte-identical, so requiring every migration task to cover it would be an obligation over a thing that did not move, and it would fail the scope check for every task that carries infra/migrations/** today. When a migration does move the output — a renamed column an existing query reads — check-sqlc-drift is what catches it, at CI, on the merge that made it true.
